scope: Theorem 1.2 (Uniform log canonical index) of the manuscript “Uniform Pluricanonical Iitaka Fibrations” (preprints/Uniform-Pluricanonical-Iitaka-Fibrations-October-3-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 034 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 88c226e29ee72119), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let d ≥ 0, and let Φ ⊂ [0, 1]∩Q satisfy the descending chain condition. There is an integer a(d, Φ) > 0 such that every projective log canonical pair (X, B) of dimension d, with boundary coefficients in Φ and KX + B ∼Q 0, satisfies a(d, Φ)(KX + B) ∼ 0. Here the multiple is an integral principal divisor, not merely a numerically trivial or rationally linearly trivial divisor.
